abbreviations.definition: adverse event: Any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product that does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment. An adverse event can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a medicinal (investigational) product, whether or not related to the medicinal (investigational) product.

A complaint is any written, electronic, or oral communication that alleges deficiencies related to the identity, quality, purity, durability, reliability, safety or effectiveness, or performance of a drug or drug delivery system.
Adherence to all study-related, good clinical practice (GCP), and applicable regulatory requirements.

clinical research physician: Individual responsible for the medical conduct of the study. Responsibilities of the CRP may be performed by a physician, clinical research scientist, global safety physician or other medical officer.
The act of assigning a patient to a treatment. Patients who are enrolled in the study are those who have been assigned to a treatment.
Patients entered into a study are those who sign the informed consent form directly or through their legally acceptable representatives.
The International Council for Harmonization of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use

A process by which a patient voluntarily confirms his or her willingness to participate in a particular study, after having been informed of all aspects of the study that are relevant to the patient’s decision to participate. Informed consent is documented by means of a written, signed, and dated informed consent form.
An interim analysis is an analysis of clinical study data, separated into treatment groups, that is conducted before the final reporting database is created/locked.

investigational product: A pharmaceutical form of an active ingredient or placebo being tested or used as a reference in a clinical trial, including products already on the market when used or assembled (formulated or packaged) in a way different from the authorized form, or marketed products used for an unauthorized indication, or marketed products used to gain further information about the authorized form.

intention to treat: The principle that asserts that the effect of a treatment policy can be best assessed by evaluating on the basis of the intention to treat a patient (that is, the planned treatment regimen) rather than the actual treatment given. It has the consequence that patients allocated to a treatment group should be followed up, assessed, and analyzed as members of that group irrespective of their compliance to the planned course of treatment.
Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite-Clinical trials
Patient Global Impression of status for physical activity
The act of determining if an individual meets minimum requirements to become part of a pool of potential candidates for participation in a clinical study.

treatment-emergent adverse event: An untoward medical occurrence that emerges during a defined treatment period, having been absent pretreatment, or worsens relative to the pretreatment state, and does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment.
Short-Form-36 Health Survey version 2, acute form

notes: Protocol version: the PDF holds one protocol version, Protocol I8F-MC-GPHK(b) (Amendment (b), approved 04-Oct-2021); the SoA (pp 18-29) and its notes come from this version. Appendix 12 (pp 126-127) only summarises Amendment (a) changes already incorporated (e.g. waist circumference added to Visit 199, 'register study visit in IWRS' added, Visit 21 window); no later amendment in the PDF changes an SoA activity, so no additional entries were made. No page reads '[no text layer on this page]'; no item is read_from page image. Rule 10: the Appendix 2 Clinical Laboratory Tests table (p 96) runs its two columns together in the text layer and was checked on the page image: Total Cholesterol, Triglycerides and Creatine kinase (CK) belong to Clinical Chemistry (the text layer places them after Urine Chemistries), Urine Chemistries holds only Albumin and Creatinine, Lipid Panel holds LDL-C, HDL-C, VLDL-C, and Insulin / C-peptide are separate headings. The Appendix 5 Hepatic Monitoring Tests table (p 109) was also checked on its page image for the panel assignment. The Hypersensitivity Tests table (p 98) is one panel and was assigned from the text layer alone. Text-layer superscripts are merged into words (e.g. 'Insuline' = Insulin with footnote e, 'Hematologya' = Hematology with footnote a); analytes are written without the footnote letters, quotes keep the text layer. Lab: p 95 states all Appendix 2 tests are performed by the central laboratory unless otherwise stated, and footnote a names a Lilly-designated central laboratory; local laboratory results are only required when central results are not available in time.
